title: And, bhikkhus, what are the things to be fully understood? Form, bhikkhus, is a thing to be fully understood; feeling is a thing to be…
content: And, bhikkhus, what are the things to be fully understood? Form, bhikkhus, is a thing to be fully understood; feeling is a thing to be fully understood; perception is a thing to be fully understood; formations are things to be fully understood; consciousness is a thing to be fully understood. These, bhikkhus, are the things to be fully understood. And, bhikkhus, what is full understanding? The destruction of greed, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion, bhikkhus, is called full understanding.

title: - Bhikkhus, form is suffering, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form,…
content: - Bhikkhus, form is suffering, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form, does not delight in future form, and for present form practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation. Bhikkhus, feeling is suffering ... perception is suffering ... formations are suffering ... Bhikkhus, consciousness is suffering, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past consciousness, does not delight in future consciousness, and for present consciousness practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a person is shot with a dart, and then they shoot him with a second dart. Thus, bhikkhus, that person experiences the…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a person is shot with a dart, and then they shoot him with a second dart. Thus, bhikkhus, that person experiences the feeling of both darts. So too, bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person, when touched by a painful feeling, sorrows, grieves, laments, beats his breast, and becomes confused. That person experiences two feelings: a bodily feeling and a mental feeling. Touched by that painful feeling, he feels aversion. Because he feels aversion towards that painful feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion towards painful feeling persists. Touched by that painful feeling, he delights in sensual pleasure. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, the unlearned ordinary person does not know any escape from painful feeling other than sensual pleasure. Delighting in that sensual pleasure, the underlying tendency to lust for pleasant feeling persists. He does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of those feelings. Because he does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of those feelings, the underlying tendency to ignorance for neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling persists. If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is bound. If he feels a painful feeling, he feels it as one who is bound. If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is bound. Bhikkhus, this is called an unlearned ordinary person who is bound by birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is bound by suffering.

title: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood. He does…
content: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood. He does not, for the sake of almsfood, engage in improper, unsuitable seeking. If he does not get almsfood, he is not worried or regretful; if he gets almsfood, he uses it without greed, infatuation, or clinging, seeing the danger and understanding the escape. He does not, because of contentment with any kind of almsfood, praise himself or disparage others. Whoever here is skilled, not lax, clearly comprehending, mindful — this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is called one who stands on the ancient, original noble tradition.

title: When this does not exist, that does not exist. With the cessation of this, that ceases. That is: With the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations…
content:
When this does not exist, that does not exist. With the cessation of this, that ceases. That is: With the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease; with the cessation of volitional formations, consciousness ceases; with the cessation of consciousness, name-and-form ceases; with the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense bases cease; with the cessation of the six sense bases, contact ceases; with the cessation of contact, feeling ceases; with the cessation of feeling, craving ceases; with the cessation of craving, clinging ceases; with the cessation of clinging, existence ceases; with the cessation of existence, birth ceases; with the cessation of birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering."

Truly, when these things
Are present and arise,
For that brahmin who is
Ardent and meditating,

Then, for that person,
All doubts are dispelled,
Since he has fully known
The cessation of conditions.

title: The Blessed One replied to Upasīva: Mindful, not longing for anything, You will cross the flood by relying on 'nothing'. Abandoning sensual desires, free from…
content:
The Blessed One replied to Upasīva:
Mindful, not longing for anything,
You will cross the flood by relying on 'nothing'.
Abandoning sensual desires, free from doubt,
Seeing the destruction of craving day and night — that is Nibbāna.

One completely free from greed for all sensual pleasures,
Relying on nothing, abandoning everything else,
Fully liberated in supreme liberation,
There that one dwells, not moving on.

Just as a flame blown by a strong wind
Goes to an end and cannot be measured,
So the sage, freed from name and body,
Goes to an end and cannot be measured.

One who has reached the end cannot be measured —
With what could one speak of him?
When all phenomena are completely uprooted,
All pathways of speech are uprooted.

title: Bhikkhus, what are the further tasks to be done? 'We must guard the sense faculties. When the eye sees a form, do not grasp the…
content: Bhikkhus, what are the further tasks to be done? 'We must guard the sense faculties. When the eye sees a form, do not grasp the general sign, do not grasp the particular sign. For whatever reason, if the eye faculty were unrestrained, covetousness, grief, evil, unwholesome states might arise, we will restrain that cause, guard the eye faculty, practice the restraint of the eye faculty. When the ear hears a sound ... nose smells an odor ... tongue tastes a flavor ... body feels a touch ... mind cognizes a mental object, do not grasp the general sign, do not grasp the particular sign. For whatever reason, if the mind faculty were unrestrained, covetousness, grief, evil, unwholesome states might arise, we will restrain that cause, guard the mind faculty, practice the restraint of the mind faculty.'

title: When it is said: 'One should not speak a secret word. One should not speak a hurtful word face to face' — for what reason…
content: When it is said: 'One should not speak a secret word. One should not speak a hurtful word face to face' — for what reason was this said? Here, bhikkhus, if one knows a secret word to be untrue, false, and unbeneficial, one should, if possible, not speak that secret word. And if one knows a secret word to be true, not false, but unbeneficial, one should train oneself not to speak it. And if one knows a secret word to be true, not false, and beneficial, then one should know the time and speak that secret word. If one knows a hurtful word face to face to be untrue, false, and unbeneficial, one should, if possible, not speak that hurtful word face to face. If one knows a hurtful word face to face to be true, not false, but unbeneficial, one should train oneself not to speak it. And if one knows a hurtful word face to face to be true, not false, and beneficial, then one should know the time and speak that hurtful word face to face.

title: It leads to his own harm, bhikkhus, when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta; it leads to the unhappiness of others, bhikkhus, when gain,…
content: It leads to his own harm, bhikkhus, when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta; it leads to the unhappiness of others, bhikkhus, when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta! Just as, bhikkhus, a banana tree, when it produces fruit, leads to its own harm; when it produces fruit, leads to the unhappiness of others. So too, bhikkhus, it leads to his own harm when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta; it leads to the unhappiness of others when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta. Just as, bhikkhus, a bamboo tree, when it produces fruit, leads to its own harm; when it produces fruit, leads to the unhappiness of others. So too, bhikkhus, it leads to his own harm when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta.

title: The taker friend, The talker friend, The flatterer, The spendthrift. These four are not friends, Knowing this, the wise avoid them, Like a dangerous path.
content:
The taker friend,
The talker friend,
The flatterer,
The spendthrift.
These four are not friends,
Knowing this, the wise avoid them,
Like a dangerous path.
